title: Jesus, My Strength, My Hope
description: Jesus, My Strength, My Hope in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 301. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, my strength, my hope, On thee I cast my care, With hum-ble con-fi-dence look_ up, And know thou hear'st my prayer. Give me on thee to wait, Till I can all things do, On thee, al-might-y to cre-ate, Al-might-y to re-new.

lines: On thee I cast my care,
And know thou hear'st my prayer.
Give me on thee to wait,
Till I can all things do,
That tramples down and casts behind
Bold to take up, firm to sustain
That looks to thee when sin is near,
For ever standing on its guard,
I want a heart to pray,
Never to murmur at thy stay,
Out of the deep on thee to call,
To thee and thy great name;
A pure desire that all may learn,
Till thou my patient spirit guide

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
